scope: Bounded read-only source and installed-SDK inspection; no VM execution, kernel build, system changes, AMD-host use, or backend implementation.

host.measurement: uname -m; sw_vers; xcrun --show-sdk-path; read-only sysctl hw.optional.arm64 kern.hv_support hw.model machdep.cpu.brand_string

findings.topic: Guest-only retired counting and counter exits
findings.result: No public arm64 API found for retired branch/instruction counters or count-triggered exits. SDK system-register enum omits PMCR/PMEV registers. QEMU HVF describes OS PMU emulation as cycles-only; its userspace implementation declares no valid PMU events. This does not establish a usable counted-preemption path.
findings.confidence: high for public API/source gap; no runtime PMU qualification
evidence: Apple's managed PMC MSR documentation concerns Intel and is not Apple Silicon support.

findings.result: Public debug exception/access traps and MDSCR/breakpoint registers exist. QEMU sets MDSCR.SS/PSTATE.SS and handles EC_SOFTWARESTEP. Useful correction primitives exist, but no whole-Linux fidelity/cost test ran and they do not supply a coarse counter.
findings.confidence: high for availability; unqualified for Seedbox Linux correction

findings.result: SDK defines CNTVCT_EL0 = mach_absolute_time() - vtimer_offset. Offset/mask/IRQ controls exist; changing an offset cannot remove host elapsed time during a running slice. No public general CNTVCT/RNDR trap selector or configurable CPU feature mask was found. HCR/MDCR/CNTHCTL EL2 registers are documented for guest EL2 enabled VMs, not unrestricted host-EL2 controls. Time/RNG instruction closure remains unqualified; no claim that RNDR is exposed on this host.
findings.confidence: high for timer relation; medium for API completeness inference

findings.result: Apple documents one VM per process. SDK permits one vCPU per thread and requires owning-thread run/register operations. A direct process holding several independent machines on one thread conflicts with D001. Serialized worker-process handshakes might retain deterministic semantic ownership but add execution threads/processes and need an explicit D001 change plus qualification.
evidence: Apple Hypervisor overview, Virtual Resource Mapping

findings.result: rr has Apple M1/M2 taken-branch event 0x90 entries using Linux PMU names, and perf_event_open counters exclude guests. These entries neither qualify this M4 nor prove macOS guest filtering/overflow access.

Arm documents exception-return clearing of exclusive state; host interruptions can therefore affect store-exclusive results independently of intended guest scheduling. rr rejects legacy LL/SC atomics and requires LSE applications. Whole-Linux support must also audit kernel/boot/library/JIT sites; application LSE alone is insufficient. This is a determinism issue separate from weak-memory exploration.
findings.confidence: high for architecture and rr restriction; host HVF behavior not measured
evidence: DeCL OSDI25 paper, instruction nondeterminism discussion

findings.result: TCG can run x86 Linux on macOS and has exact instruction budgets, fixed progress-to-time conversion and deterministic idle jumps. It avoids hardware PMU/ARM guest admission work. Stock QEMU still has support threads and externally timed inputs; icount is not complete seeded world integration. A TCG backend needs explicit scheduling/device/input ownership and instruction-count profile qualification. No slowdown was measured.
evidence: QEMU invocation: -icount fixed shift, align=off, sleep=off

recommendation.native_hvf: Park now. Public counted-preemption and time closure gaps plus VM/thread topology make it unlikely to accelerate the current AMD/KVM integration milestone. Debug support alone is not decisive.
recommendation.tcg: Keep only as a bounded future measurement candidate, not a competing implementation. Old 100-1000x estimates are unmeasured and cannot reject it under O5.
recommendation.minimal_decisive_test: Later cap a TCG feasibility spike at 1-2 hours: reuse compatible retained x86 Linux/initramfs inputs with one vCPU, fixed icount shift, align=off, sleep=off, fixed RTC and pinned CPU/device profile; no record/replay prerequisite or external network. Compare five fresh runs at a deterministic guest boundary using application/clock/entropy witnesses and CPU/RAM state, and measure boot separately from a bounded concurrent race fixture with atomic control. Failure of input closure or practical wall time parks it; passing establishes a candidate only, not multi-machine Seedbox support. Do not assume KVM snapshots are portable to TCG. No such test ran in this inspection.

limits: Remote master sources are inspected snapshots, not locally pinned commits.
No running guest, RNG exposure, nested PMU, Linux fidelity, performance or multi-machine experiment was performed.
No relevant project memory was found; conclusions rely on current headers, docs and primary sources.
